S1: Nitrogen distributions under four prompt designs in the African sample. (a) Mean nitrogen rates, (b) distribution similarity, defined as one minus the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic, and (c) the percentage of predictions at or above the observed 90th percentile (P90). All model summaries use the same 275 profiles with observed nitrogen rates. Dashed lines mark the observed mean in (a), the distribution-only reference in (b), and the observed percentage at or above P90 in (c). The archived distribution-only reference averages 400 draws of 280 values from a zero-inflated lognormal distribution fitted to the 275 observed rates; values are assigned independently of farmer characteristics.
S2: Variation in simulated nitrogen and labor inputs across African prompt designs. Ratios of simulated to observed standard deviations (SD; a, c and e) and 90th percentiles (P90; b, d and f) are shown for nitrogen, family labor and hired labor. The matched samples contain 275, 278 and 275 profiles, respectively. Dashed lines indicate equal simulated and observed variation or percentile values. Points summarize the three interfaces under T1–T4, with lines connecting designs within each interface.
S3: Country-specific agreement between predicted and observed nitrogen rates under four prompt designs. Pearson correlations are shown separately for Ethiopia, Malawi, Nigeria and Tanzania using all profiles with observed nitrogen rates in each country. Symbols identify the three interfaces, and lines connect T1–T4. Dotted lines mark zero correlation. These panels describe differences among the four survey countries; they do not represent the paired country-label intervention.
S4: Percentile ratios of simulated to observed inputs in the African sample. Panels show nitrogen, family labor and hired labor for the matched samples of 275, 278 and 275 profiles. At each percentile, the solid line is the median ratio across the 12 interface–prompt configurations, and the shaded band spans their minimum and maximum. Percentiles from 5 to 99 were evaluated; ratios are displayed only where the observed percentile exceeds 28% of the observed 90th percentile, following the archived plotting rule to avoid unstable ratios near zero. Dashed lines indicate equal simulated and observed percentile values. The band describes configurations, not sampling uncertainty.
S5: Empirical distributions of nitrogen rates in the African sample. Each panel compares T1–T4 predictions from one interface with observed rates for the same 275 profiles. Curves include zero-use records and retain the full observed and simulated range. Differences in the curves therefore show both the fraction of non-users and the distribution of positive rates.
